name: Ramsau im Zillertal
kurzbeschreibung: High-altitude scattered settlement in the Zillertal with untouched countryside and stunning hiking trails.
text:
Überblick

Ramsau im Zillertal is located in the upper Zillertal valley within the Schwaz district at an altitude of 604 metres, counting around 1,735 residents. The municipal area spans the valley floor on the eastern bank of the Ziller River and ascends across forested slopes to the summit of the Hochfeld at 2,350 metres. Alongside Hippach and Schwendau, it constitutes the vibrant centre of the Mayrhofen-Hippach holiday region. Ramsau delights visitors with warm hospitality, a strategic position close to major ski resorts, and the breathtaking scenery of the Zillertal Alps.

Geschichte

Ramsau was first documented in 1188. For centuries, the valley was partitioned: lands east of the Ziller belonged to the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg, whereas the western side belonged to Tyrol. Only in 1816 did the Salzburg territory permanently merge into Tyrol and Austria. Founded in 1817 as Ramsberg after the hillside mountain hamlets, the community was officially renamed Ramsau im Zillertal in 1978. The picturesque parish church of the Seven Sorrows of Mary, known as the Ramsauer Kirchl, was erected between 1841 and 1843 on the Birgler hill following religious tensions. The inauguration of the Zillertalbahn railway in 1901 heralded the start of modern tourism.

Anreise

Travelling to Ramsau im Zillertal is straightforward. Motorists take the Inntalautobahn A12 to the Wiesing/Zillertal exit and follow the B169 Zillertalstraße south for roughly 25 kilometres directly to the town. Train travellers transfer at Jenbach main station onto the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn, which runs every half hour and stops conveniently at the Ramsau-Hippach station. Frequent local buses and winter ski shuttles link the station directly to Mayrhofen, cable cars, and romantic tributary valleys.

Tipps

An absolute highlight for visitors is the Gerlossteinbahn cable car on neighboring Hainzenberg, offering a via ferrata on the Gerlossteinwand and the Almflieger zip line in summer. During winter, it hosts Tyrol's longest natural toboggan run, stretching 7 kilometres with evening floodlighting. From Ramsau, road travellers can access the panoramic Zillertaler Höhenstraße alpine road climbing above 2,000 metres. Cyclists appreciate the flat Zillertal-Radweg trail following the river. Food lovers must taste authentic Zillertaler Krapfen pastries filled with tangy Graukäse cheese.
